subject.title: [Feature]: Improve `openclaw config` to avoid secrets and invalid files

question: Should bare interactive `openclaw config` change from the documented configure wizard to help output, and should literal writes to known secret config paths warn or fail in favor of SecretRefs?
rationale: The remaining work changes a documented CLI setup contract and credential-handling policy, so automation should not choose the compatibility and secret-safety boundary alone.

options.title: Add Narrow Guardrails
options.body: Show help for bare `openclaw config` on already-configured systems while preserving `openclaw configure` and `--section`, and warn or fail only for registry-known secret literal writes with a clear SecretRef path.

options.title: Keep Current Contract
options.body: Leave bare `openclaw config` as the wizard and rely on docs, validation, SecretRef builders, dry-run, and placeholder restoration for safer usage.

options.title: Go Strict SecretRef-First
options.body: Fail closed for literal writes to supported secret targets, accepting stronger default security with higher upgrade and script compatibility impact.

recommendation.title: Add Narrow Guardrails
recommendation.body: Show help for bare `openclaw config` on already-configured systems while preserving `openclaw configure` and `--section`, and warn or fail only for registry-known secret literal writes with a clear SecretRef path.
